facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The patient presents with 3 months of hematochezia and two to three loose bowel movements per day with mixed blood.
The patient is intermittently neutropenic and has multiple semisessile, nonbleeding polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa.
The patient is receiving maintenance therapy and has colonoscopy findings consistent with colitis.
A small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted on examination.
The patient has chronic hematochezia and colonoscopy findings consistent with inflammation.
The histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains, suggesting calcification.

It explains the presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes, which are characteristic of Malakoplakia, in a patient with a history of T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and negative stool studies.

rationales.F01: T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia is not directly related to the listed concepts.
rationales.F02: Maintenance therapy may contribute to neutropenic colitis or chemotherapy-induced colitis.
rationales.F03: Hematochezia is a key symptom of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F04: Loose bowel movements with mixed blood are consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F09: A small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid is a possible cause of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F11: Colonoscopy findings are consistent with multiple concepts, including gastrointestinal bleeding and neutropenic colitis.
rationales.F12: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes is highly suggestive of calciphylaxis or malakoplakia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of histiocytes with basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains is highly specific for Malakoplakia, which outweighs the other findings.
